newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq to raise $100 million from banks.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq to raise $100 million from banks.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom will be raising $100 million from an international consortium of banks on terms yet to be finalised, a spokesman for the company said on Tuesday.
The syndicate will be led by Switzerland's UBS, Germany's Dresdner Bank and Japan's Fuji Bank and will be for a period of seven years. The loan will be without guarantees.
The signing is scheduled to take place in March.

Bezeq President Yitzhak Kaul said in a statement that he saw the loan and the consortium as a vote of confidence in Bezeq by the international banking community. He said the proceeds would be used to finance continued growth of Bezeq's network, improved technology and new services.
This will mark the fourth overseas syndicated borrowing by Bezeq, which is 76 percent-owned by the Israeli government and is the country's main telecommunications carrier.

Bezeq raised $150 million in October 1995, $200 million in March 1996 and another $150 million in October 1996, all for a period of five years. The last loan carried interest of Libor plus 0.3 percent.
